Summarise environmental values along tracks

Source: R/extract_to_track.R
extract_to_track.Rd

Samples points along each track, such as a dive or a vessel route, reads the value at each sample, and summarises the samples of each track. It is a convenience wrapper over the three steps of an analysis, and the workflow article shows the same steps written out:

Usage

extract_to_track(
  data,
  nc,
  var = NULL,
  track_col = NULL,
  sampling = NULL,
  spacing_km = NULL,
  depth_step_m = NULL,
  time_step = NULL,
  time_unit = c("hours", "minutes", "seconds", "days", "months", "years"),
  max_samples = 100000L,
  horizontal_radius_km = 0,
  depth_radius_m = 0,
  method = NULL,
  statistic = "mean",
  weighting = c("distance", "duration", "equal"),
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  depth_col = "depth",
  date_col = "date",
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  output_col = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Vertices of the tracks, in the order they were travelled: a data frame, matrix, named list or sf POINT object. sf points are transformed to longitude and latitude. To use sf lines, convert them first, e.g. with as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(lines, 4326))) and lon_col = "X", lat_col = "Y", track_col = "L1".

nc

The data: a netCDF file path, several paths for a series of files on one grid, an open ncdf4::nc_open() connection, or a SpatProxy from as_proxy().

var

Name of the variable, for a netCDF source. NULL detects the only data variable of the file.

track_col

Column with track IDs. NULL (default) reads all of data as one track, with ID "1". Each track needs at least two vertices.

sampling, spacing_km, depth_step_m, time_step, time_unit, max_samples

Where the samples go along each track, as in sample_3d(): only the vertices (default without a step), or with a spacing in kilometres or a depth or time step, points in between as well.

horizontal_radius_km

Radius of a circle around each sample, in kilometres, below 10000 as in buffer_3d(). 0 (default) reads the value at the sample itself. A buffer needs cells with a width, so data with a single longitude or latitude and no cell bounds (a station or a transect) takes no radius.

depth_radius_m

Distance in metres above and below each sample's depth, for the buffers. Needed with a radius for a variable with depth, and used only with a radius.

method

For a variable with depth and no radius, the depth level each sample takes, as in extract(): "nearest" (default; the level nearest the sample's depth that has a value), "nearest_level" (the nearest level, even if it has no value), "bottom" (the deepest level with a value) or "surface". Leave NULL with a radius; for a variable without depth, leave NULL or use "2d".

statistic

One or more of "mean" (default), "sd", "min" and "max", of the samples of each track.

weighting

How each sample is weighted in the track summaries: "distance" (default) by support_km, "duration" by support_seconds (needs dates), or "equal".

lon_col, lat_col, depth_col, date_col

Vertex columns. The depth is needed for a variable with depth, unless method is "bottom" or "surface", and for depth_step_m. The date is needed for data with dated time steps, for time_step and for duration weights. Dates and date-times are read as in as_vector3d().

lon_dim, lat_dim, depth_dim, time_dim

Dimension names for a netCDF source, as in as_proxy().

time_match, max_time_diff

How a sample's time is matched to a time step, as in as_voxel(): the nearest step (default) or an exact one, and the largest gap in days for a nearest match.

output_col

Name of the value column in samples. NULL uses the variable's name.

Value

A list of two data frames:

  • samples: one row per sample, in order along each track, with track_id, sample_id, the position (in lon_col and lat_col, with longitudes from -180 to 180), the depth and date when used (in depth_col and date_col; dates stay dates), distance_km from the track's start, support_km, support_seconds, is_interpolated (FALSE for the track's own vertices), and the value in output_col. With a radius, also <output>_n, the number of values in the sample's buffer.

  • summary: one row per track, with track_id, a column per statistic, and n, the number of samples with a value.

Details

  1. Build: the vertices of each track become a line with as_vector3d(), and sample_3d() places points along it, with depth and time interpolated between vertices. With horizontal_radius_km, buffer_3d() turns each sample into a buffer.

  2. Intersect: without a radius, extract() reads the value at each sample, in the cell that holds it and at the depth level method picks. With a radius, the data for the sample's time step are read with crop() and as_voxel() (or rast() for a variable without depth), and mask() keeps the values inside its buffer: the cells the circle touches, and the levels whose slab of water overlaps the depth window. summarise_3d() gives their mean, weighted by cell volume.

  3. Summarise: the statistics of each track's sample values, each sample weighted by weighting.

Each sample is matched to the time step nearest its time, or equal to it with time_match = "exact", as extract() matches points: a date by its UTC day, a date-time as an instant. A sample gets NA when it is outside the grid, on a cell or level without a value, has no date on data with dated time steps, or has no time step that matches. One warning counts these samples, by reason. The track summaries leave them out, and n is the number of samples with a value.

With weighting = "distance" each sample stands for half the distance to the samples either side (support_km), so a stretch sampled more densely doesn't count for more; with "duration" for half the time (support_seconds). The weighted standard deviation is the one summarise_3d() uses. A track whose samples all have zero weight, such as a track that doesn't move with distance weights, gets equal weights. Neighbouring samples are usually correlated, so the standard deviation describes their spread, not the uncertainty of the mean.

See also

sample_3d(), extract_to_point(), extract_to_buffer(), and the workflow article.

Examples

# Daily temperature on a 10 x 10 grid of 1 degree cells at four depths.
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".nc")
lon <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("lon", "degrees_east", seq(0.5, 9.5))
lat <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("lat", "degrees_north", seq(0.5, 9.5))
depth <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("depth", "m", c(5, 15, 30, 60))
time <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("time", "days since 2020-01-01", 0:2)
temp <- ncdf4::ncvar_def("temp", "degree_Celsius",
                         list(lon, lat, depth, time), -9999)
nc <- ncdf4::nc_create(path, temp)
ncdf4::ncvar_put(nc, temp, seq_len(10 * 10 * 4 * 3) / 10)
ncdf4::nc_close(nc)

# A dive from the surface to 50 m over two days.
dive <- data.frame(lon = c(2.5, 6.5), lat = c(3.5, 5.5), depth = c(0, 50),
                   date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-03")))

# The value at a sample at least every 50 km, and the mean along the dive.
track <- extract_to_track(dive, path, spacing_km = 50)
track$summary
#>   track_id mean  n
#> 1        1   42 11

# The mean within 30 km and 10 m above and below each sample instead.
extract_to_track(dive, path, spacing_km = 50, horizontal_radius_km = 30,
                 depth_radius_m = 10)$summary
#>   track_id    mean  n
#> 1        1 44.2459 11
